scope: Native module carving pointer widths, alignment fallback and range phase

checks: Four-byte back-reference excludes nonzero neighboring bytes
Known misaligned modules trigger one-byte stride for both pointer widths
Unaligned lower range boundary preserves the reference range(lower, end, alignment) phase for both widths

limitations: These are native synthetic regression cases and a pinned source comparison, not actual-reference execution vectors for full hidden module scanning.
ISF member size controls the back-reference read; ISF pointer size controls alignment. Both are restricted to four or eight bytes.
The existing two-page window, cancellation, scan budget, partial diagnostics and back-offset bound remain in force.
Real Linux32 discovery and extraction are not established; the public Linux32 ISF parse gate remains closed.
No full plugin contract is established by this batch.
